adjudication.notes: The source explicitly excludes server-only advisories because the bot does not run the server component; package presence alone is not reachability.

evidence-points: application does not run the affected server component

payload.excerpt: ion reuse | | CVE-2026-54279 | LOW | 3.14.1 | Host-only cookies become domain cookies after CookieJar persistence | The remaining 60 are aiohttp.web server-side (static file handler, multipart parsing, clientmaxsize) and genuinely do not apply — this bot runs no HTTP server. Not padding the count. Why the pin is the problem discord.py 2.7.1 declares aiohttp>=3.7.4,<4 — a wide range that happily accepts a current version. The hand-pin in requirements.txt is the only thing holding aiohttp at 3.10.10. Removing the pin and letting the resolver take ≥3.14.3 resolves all of them in one move. aiohttp is not imported anywhere in this codebase (grep confirms) — it's purely transitive, and pinning transitive dependencies by hand is what created the exposure. Also: Black carries a HIGH CVE and is a runtime dependency OSV returns 3 advisories for black==24.10.0: - CVE-2026-32274 — HIGH, arbitrary file writes from unsanitized input in the cache filename.
